title: Streaming resilience: sequence markers, chunk reconciliation, and tool-call safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Scope: Implement a robust SSE-compatible streaming layer that uses explicit sequence markers and per-chunk checksums to support reliable reconnects, deterministic chunk reconciliation, and safe handling of function/tool calls during partial replays. This ticket covers server-side framing changes, client compatibility hints, and operational rollout strategy.

Goals:
- Add a compact per-event header schema (sequence marker + chunk-index + checksum) to allow clients to detect duplicates, gaps, and reordering across reconnects.
- Define a server-side reconciliation strategy that allows replay up to but not including already-delivered tool invocations unless they are idempotent or have dedupe tokens.
- Ensure function/tool calling semantics are preserved on reconnect: avoid double-invocation of external tools while still delivering consistent transcript to the client.
- Provide a graceful compatibility mode for older clients through negotiated capability headers and a short-lived shim behavior.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement new client SDKs (separate SDK tasks).
- It does not change the high-level API for structured outputs or function signatures; it augments transport framing only.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- We prefer a small wire format (avoid large envelopes per chunk) to keep latency low, but we need enough metadata to guarantee safety for tool calls. Using a 64-bit sequence + 32-bit chunk index + CRC32 checksum gives a small overhead (~16 bytes) with good detection.
- There is a trade-off between server-maintained replay state (expensive) and stateless resume tokens (compact). We will issue short-lived resume tokens that encode last-seen sequence and a lease ID; the server keeps a bounded lease map for 5 minutes to allow efficient, authoritative replay.
- For tool-call safety we require invocation_id on every function/tool call event. The server will dedupe calls for identical invocation_id within the replay window. Clients are required to attach idempotency tokens for any side-effecting calls to be safe beyond the server lease window.

Out-of-scope but related work: integration with Dedicated routing policies for fallback and private deployment KMS for invocation token signing (follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: SSE stream events include sequence_marker, chunk_index, and checksum fields and are small overhead (< 32B/evt).
Client can reconnect and request replay from a resume_token; server replays events starting at next unacknowledged sequence except for deduped tool invocations.
Tool/function call events include an invocation_id; server replays transcript without re-executing calls whose invocation_id was already executed within the lease window.
Backward compatibility: older clients (no capability header) can still connect and receive streams via a shim that emits legacy JSONL frames for 30 days post-rollout.
A performance regression benchmark (50th/95th token latency) shows < 8% overhead compared to current runtime on typical prompt workloads.
Comprehensive integration test: chaotic reconnect test passes (10k simulated reconnects with network partitions) with no spurious duplicate external tool invocations recorded in logs.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial ticket created following on-call incident where a reconnect caused duplicated webhook triggers for a small number of sessions. See incident notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/SSE+reconnect+incident+2025-02-09

2025-02-14 - Jonah Kim: Spike summary uploaded: lightweight seq markers (u64) + chunk index (u32) + CRC32 checksums appear to detect all observed corruption modes in our fuzz harness. Spike doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1sE-stream-spike

2025-02-18 - Design feedback (Lina Morales): Prefer an explicit 'invocation_id' field on tool events and require clients to send idempotency_token for externally visible side-effects. This avoids server needing global side-effect logs. Added to ACs.

2025-02-20 - Eng review (Rajiv Singh): Raised concern about server lease memory; suggest bounded LRU map keyed by lease id that stores last N seqs per session. Jonah to prototype. Referenced PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345

2025-02-26 - Jonah Kim: Prototype implemented in runtime branch 'streaming/seq-markers'. Basic server-side lease map uses 5-minute TTL and stores last 200 sequence entries per session. Microbench results: 2% extra CPU at 1000 rps on c6i-equivalent nodes.

2025-03-02 - QA (Maya Chen): Fuzz harness runs (10k sessions, random disconnects). Found edge case: chunk_index wrap-around at very long single-event encodings (not expected). Decided mitigation: chunk_index is 32-bit and we will add defensive checks to reject >1e7 chunks per event and log for investigation.

2025-03-04 - Security (Theo Alvarez): Reviewed idempotency guidance; recommend signing invocation_id with session-scoped HMAC when used across private routing to prevent replay attack vectors. Follow-up security ticket suggested.

2025-03-05 - Jonah Kim: Preparing PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12789. Includes server framing changes, resume token issuance, and an opt-in capability negotiation header 'X-RW-Stream-V: 2'. Requesting review from Lina, Rajiv, and Theo.
test_plan: Unit tests for framing encoder/decoder (seq+chunk+crc) with fuzz-generated payloads.
Integration: end-to-end reconnect replay test with simulated client that randomly drops connection and requests resume tokens.
Chaos: long-duration (48h) simulated production traffic with DNS flaps and partitioned network; verify no duplicate external calls in audit logs.
Performance: compare token latency 50/95/99th vs baseline using loadbench and record CPU/GPU impact.
Upgrade path: staged rollout to 10% of hosts behind a feature flag, enable compatibility shim for older clients, ramp to 100% in two weeks if metrics OK.
notes: Implementation detail: resume_token format = base64(lease_id || last_seq || mac); lease kept in server with TTL=300s. If lease expired server will return a conservative 'cannot-replay' response and client must reconnect from fresh start.

Client expectations: SDKs should expose 'onResumePossible' callback with resume_token and a method 'requestReplay(token)' to explicitly ask for replay; streaming raw HTTP clients can pass 'Resume-Token' header. SDK task will follow.
Compatibility: legacy clients will be served a JSONL 'legacy_frame' envelope until shim deprecation date. Telemetry will include capability negotiation stats to track adoption.
